text:
Maria: Quick sync — I ran a short workshop with a couple customers yesterday and want to lock down the observability sprint scope. Goal: land a lightweight Console surface for per-route cost + an error-analytics MVP, plus tracing hooks and sampling policy that are safe to roll out. Proposed pilot: internal + 1 external customer (Acme). Thoughts? :thinking_face:

Kevin: +1 on pilot. We need a clear sampling strategy though — full traces for hot paths, sampled spans for the rest. If we do full traces for top-5 routes we estimate ~20-30% increase in trace volume. Need to map that to storage/export costs.

Anya: Ops note — we must include a backpressure/fallback so exporters don't block requests. Also recommend a per-tenant daily spend SLI (e.g. trace_cost_per_day < $X) before we auto-disable heavy sampling.

Phil: From a data perspective, propose retention tiers: 7d for full traces, 30d for spans summary, 90d for error fingerprints. Rough calc: at 1M requests/day with 5% full traces, 7d full trace retention ≈ 120GB. That maps to ~$2k/mo in infra for one medium customer (ballpark). I'll add numbers for Acme.

Lina: For Console UI, keep MVP small: (1) per-route cost breakdown widget (top 10 routes by monthly spend), (2) error heatmap showing counts + percentage of requests impacted, (3) a trace link from error rows to the trace viewer. No fancy drilldowns for MVP.

Maria: Draft acceptance criteria (proposed):
- Per-route cost view in Console (top-10 routes, daily/weekly aggregation)
- Tracing hooks & a sampling policy editor (JSON) in Console with hot-route override
- Error analytics: top-10 errors with fingerprinting and trace link
- Canary plan: internal >1 org for 48h, then Acme pilot for 7 days
- SLOs: enabling sampling must not increase request p95 latency >2%

Kevin: Implementation sketch (config example):
```json
{
  "hot_routes": ["/v1/generate", "/v1/chat"],
  "hot_route_full_pct": 100,
  "global_sample_pct": 1,
  "adaptive_reservoir": {"target_per_minute": 50}
}
```
This gives deterministic full tracing for hot routes and very light sampling elsewhere. We'll need feature flags to flip per-org.

Anya: Ops roll-out checklist highlights:
- Backpressure: drop spans when exporter queue > 5k
- Canary gating metric: trace_export_latency < 200ms and trace_export_queue < 1000
- Fallback: auto-switch to span-only mode if exporter fails for >5m

Maria: Decision proposal for today: proceed with hot-route full trace + adaptive reservoir for others, pilot with Acme, UI limited to the 3 widgets Lina suggested. Owners: Kevin (runtime + runbook), Anya (ops gating + canary), Phil (cost model), Lina (UI mockups). Deliver runbook + cost estimates by EOD Friday. @Kevin please confirm ETA. :+1:

Kevin: Confirmed. I'll post the runbook, canary playbook, and a rough cost worksheet by Friday EOD. Will include an A/B where we try full traces for top-3 vs top-5 routes to compare cost/diagnostic value.

OpsBot: deploy-bot: canary rollout scheduled -> org:redwood-internal, start: 2025-06-02T09:00Z, duration: 48h.

Maria: Great — thanks team. I'll follow up with Acme onboarding note and sample dataset for Phil. If anyone has objections to the acceptance criteria above, speak now or DM me. :rocket:
